unruled:dependent#1.evidence: low, batched in T-092. Repeat of round-3 dependent#3 (r3 L1), widened to the whole support list of p501 pp. 15 and 20-21. Covered in substance by dependent.supported: lodging at fair rental value (the person's own home, and lodging they give you, are theirs), own funds actually spent (savings, tax-exempt income, borrowed amounts), the dependency allotment, care payments you make (care you pay for is support you provide). Arithmetic of the over-half test: household-expense division, fair market value, capital items. Rare: fiscal year, borrowed money repaid later, lump-sum home-for-the-aged payment, foster-care expenses of a business or charitable caregiver, one check to both spouses, GI Bill. Not in the question and plausible: medical insurance premiums you pay are your support and Medicare and other insurance benefits are not (p501 p. 21; r3 L1); income and social security taxes the person pays, life insurance premiums and funeral expenses are not support (p501 p. 21), so a filer who counts a parent's life insurance premiums or funeral costs as support may cross the over-half line. Support-definition omissions are Low, as round-1 PENDING-8 and r3 L1.

unruled:dependent#2.evidence: low, batched in T-092. Repeat of round-3 dependent#4 (r3 L2), which named state benefits, GI Bill and DEA payments. dependent.self_support carries own funds actually spent (which covers savings, tax-exempt income and borrowed amounts spent), lodging at fair rental value (which covers a home the person owns), foster payments, scholarships and social security. Arithmetic: capital items. Not in the question: GI Bill amounts are in total support, DEA payments used for the child's support are excluded, Medicare and insurance benefits are not support, and income and social security taxes the person pays from their own income are not support (p501 p. 21). The tax rule needs a working child whose withheld taxes would carry them past half their own support; GI Bill and DEA students are rare. Low.

unruled:dependent#3.evidence: Repeat of round-3 dependent#1 (r3 N1): the non-taxpayer carve-out (i1040gi p. 19; p501 p. 18) is absent from dependent.other_claimant, but a Yes refuses, through the refusal on dependent.qualifying_child, which reaches the qualifying-relative path. Witness rerun on the current tree (stage8.hoh.parent.test1 filed single; /tmp/adj-compl-r4/w/q_single*): other_claimant No gives line 19 $500; Yes gives the refusal 'Qualifying child of more than one person (tie-breaker rules)' on line 19 and household.hoh_eligible. An over-refusal, never a wrong amount.

unruled:dependent#4.evidence: open as T-091 (item 1, round-1 PENDING-4); repeat of round-3 dependent#2. On a joint return a relative of either spouse counts (p501 p. 19), but dependent.relationship feeds the qualifying-child and qualifying-relative tests alike, so the fix needs logic. The spouse's-stepparent sentence arises only on a married filing separately return, which is refused (s3.mfs, scope.ready).

unruled:dependent#5.evidence: open as T-091 (item 2, round-1 PENDING-7); repeat of round-3 dependent#6. The reasonable-return condition (p501 p. 9) and the indefinite nursing-home stay (p501 p. 19) pull dependent.months (and part_year_home) in opposite directions for head of household and the qualifying-relative household test. Keeping up the home during the absence is household.home_cost (Test 2, 'for 2025') or dependent.parent_home_paid (Test 1). New in this round, and covered in substance: a required hospital stay after birth is a temporary absence for medical care, which dependent.months counts as time lived with you.

unruled:dependent#6.evidence: Repeat of round-3 dependent#5: dependent.student asks whether the person was enrolled as a full-time student at a school, including a technical, trade or mechanical school. A co-op student is enrolled in the school's regular course, of which the co-op job is part, so the plain answer is Yes; the on-the-job-training exclusion concerns training courses, not a school's co-op. 'Enrolled as a full-time student' is naturally read by the school's own standard, which is the second quoted sentence.

unruled:dependent#7.evidence: low, batched in T-092. Repeat of round-3 dependent#8 (r3 L3). dependent.divorced_rule asks whether a Form 8332 release or a decree lets the noncustodial parent claim the child, and a Yes refuses (dependent.qualifying_child). It does not say that a revocation counts for 2025 only if written notice was given in 2024 or earlier (p501 pp. 14-15); a custodial parent who revoked in 2025 plausibly answers No when the release still holds and the answer should be Yes (refusal). The attachment of the revocation is a paper entry. Rare: it needs a release revoked in 2025 specifically.

unruled:dependent#8.evidence: Repeat of round-3 dependent#9: dc_paid asks only for expenses for the person's care so that the filer could work or look for work, which carries the daily allocation for part-period work and the division of mixed-purpose expenses; chauffeur, bartender and gardener services are not care of the person. Child support goes to a child who does not live with the payer, who is then not the payer's qualifying person (dependent.dc_qp).

unruled:dependent#9.evidence: Repeat of round-3 dependent#10: f8863.ban asks about a denial or reduction after 2015 needing Form 8862 and the 2- and 10-year bans, and f8863.ban_refused refuses Form 8863 line 7. The HANDLED ELSEWHERE list still misses it because the refusal is on f8863.line7, which reads dependent only through other f8863 lines.

unruled:dependent#10.evidence: low, batched in T-092. New. The American opportunity credit needs the student's TIN issued by the due date (i8863 pp. 1 and 3); dependent.edu_student reads dependent.tin, which also answers Yes for an ITIN or ATIN merely applied for by then (the Step 3 and credit-for-other-dependents standard; amb.2025.ctc_spouse_itin_application confines the deeming of an applied-for ITIN to the credit for other dependents). Witness (stage19.example.jack_kay; /tmp/adj-compl-r4/w/e_*): tin Yes gives line 29 $1,000 and Form 8863 line 19 $1,500; No refuses the return (dependent.claimed_no_tin), so a student with an ITIN applied for but not issued gets the credit wrongly and no answer is right. Rare: a dependent student who needs an ITIN and whose application is pending at the due date; the same rarity as round-1 PENDING-10 (expired ITIN, Low).

unruled:household#1.evidence: Low, batched in T-092. p501 p. 9, Note: TANF or similar payments you received and used to support another person are support you provided. household.home_cost (BUG-0260) states the included and excluded costs and the own-funds rule but not TANF; a filer whose TANF grant is issued for the child may read the own-funds sentence as making the rent paid from it the child's and answer No. A No ends in a refusal at household.hoh_fails when no other test is met, never a wrong amount (stage8.hoh.child.ctc with home_cost false: lines 12e, 16 and 24 refused at household.hoh_fails; /tmp/adj-fixr5-household-refund/). Repeat of fix round 4 L1 (.transcription/proposed/fixr4/household.findings.md); see r5.findings.md and .transcription/proposed/fixr5/household.findings.md L1.

unruled:household#2.evidence: Low, batched in T-092. Two sentences. (1) The TANF note of p501 p. 9 is missing from test 4 of household.qss_eligible, as in household#1; a wrong No ends in a refusal at household.qss_fails (stage21.pending1.qss_valid_computes with qss_eligible false: lines 12e, 16 and 24 refused), never a wrong amount. (2) The name of an unclaimed qualifying child (i1040gi p. 15) is a page-1 paper entry, presentation, as round-4 household#4; the child condition itself is in test 2 of the question. See r5.findings.md.

unruled:household#3.evidence: Repeat of round-4 household#3 (and round-3 household#3): the name of an unclaimed qualifying child is a paper entry beside the head of household box (i1040gi p. 14). The tool already lets such a child qualify the filer (dependent.hoh_test2) and produces no page-1 name entries.

unruled:household#4.evidence: Repeat of round-4 household#2 (r3 N1, r4 N1): household.credit_disallowed omits the exceptions to filing Form 8862 (i1040gi pp. 39 and 43, i1040s8812 p. 2), so a filer within one answers Yes literally and is refused through eic.credit and s8812.line12. An over-refusal, never a wrong amount; carried as in r4 N1.

unruled:f2441#1.evidence: low, batched in T-092. Covered in substance by dependent.dc_paid (the column (d) amount summed by f2441.paid_total), whose question excludes food, lodging, education, clothing and entertainment, schooling for kindergarten or above, overnight camp, summer school and tutoring, out-of-home care for a person other than a dependent under 13 who does not spend 8 hours a day in your home, an unregulated dependent care center, expenses claimed as medical expenses and state social services reimbursements, counts prepaid 2024 care in 2025 (p503 p. 10), and asks only for care 'while they were a qualifying person' and 'so that you (and your spouse, if filing jointly) could work or look for work' (the day-by-day status and work-period rules in substance). Not stated: child support payments (i2441 p. 2; paid by a noncustodial parent, whose child is refused through dependent.divorced_rule or is not a qualifying person), the division of a partly work-related expense, and the household-services exclusions of a chauffeur, bartender or gardener (the question asks only for the person's care). Each needs an unusual entry to change an amount.

unruled:f2441#2.evidence: A noncustodial parent entitled to claim the child under the rule for children of divorced or separated parents (i2441 p. 1) answers dependent.divorced_rule yes, which dependent.qualifying_child refuses ('The rule for children of divorced or separated parents is outside this tool'); a custodial parent who cannot claim the child is f2441.nondependent, refused by f2441.nondependent_gate. The rest is covered: dependent.dc_qp requires a dependent qualifying child (dependent.qualifying_child includes dependent.lived_half) or a disabled dependent who lived with you more than half the year (dependent.dc_disabled_qp, dependent.dc_lived_half); the SSN, ITIN or ATIN is dependent.tin, and a dependent without one is refused by dependent.claimed_no_tin, which also refuses a child born and died in 2025 without an SSN (the 'Died' entry and attachments are paper presentation).

unruled:f2441#3.evidence: Benefits from your own sole proprietorship are refused by sc.special ('contributions you made on your own behalf, as a self-employed person, to a dependent care assistance program (Form 2441, Parts I and III)', refused at sc.screened), and partnership benefits (Schedule K-1 box 13 code O) by scope.schedule1 ('partnerships ... (Schedule E or a Schedule K-1)', refused at f1040.line8). On every computed return line 12 is the employee benefits of Form W-2 box 10 less the part in box 1 (i2441 p. 5, Line 12), the render rulings of rounds 4 and hardening (line 12, scope).

unruled:f2441#4.evidence: p503 p. 10 (self-employed treated as employer and employee; no exclusion from wages) applies only to benefits from your own business: sole-proprietorship benefits are refused by sc.special and partnership benefits by scope.schedule1, so on every computed return the line 22 answer is No and line 22 is zero, as the line's note says (Form 2441 line 22).

unruled:f2441#5.evidence: Line 24 is the smallest of lines 20, 21 and 22, and line 22 is zero on every computed return (own sole-proprietorship benefits refused by sc.special, partnership benefits by scope.schedule1), so line 24 is zero and there is no deductible amount to carry to Schedule C line 14, Schedule E line 19 or 28 or Schedule F line 15 (i2441 p. 5, Line 24).

unruled:f2441#6.evidence: Optional-method net earnings (i2441 p. 4; p503 p. 11) arise only when Schedule SE Part II is used, and person.se_screen asks 'electing an optional method (Schedule SE Part II)', refused through person.se_screened. On the remaining returns person.eic_se (Schedule SE line 3 less the Schedule 1 line 15 deduction) is the self-employment part of person.dc_earned (line 4).

unruled:f2441#7.evidence: Column (c) entries are asked per provider by dcprov.tin_kind: tin (the provider's SSN, ITIN or EIN), tax_exempt ('Tax-Exempt'), lafcp ('LAFCP' for a foreign provider of a filer living abroad), see_statement and employer (i2441 p. 3, Column (c) and U.S. citizens and resident aliens living abroad). The 'none' entry in column (a) for a Part III-only filer is a paper entry that changes no amount (presentation).

unruled:f2441#8.evidence: The employer option of dcprov.tin_kind states the i2441 p. 3 entries for employer-furnished care: 'enter "See W-2" in column (b), leave column (c) blank and enter -0- in column (e)', and dcprov.paid says 'zero if your employer furnished the care'. Care your employer paid a third party for is entered as that provider with the amount paid: dcprov.paid includes 'amounts your employer paid to the provider on your behalf' (i2441 p. 3, Column (e)), and f2441.employer_care asks only whether the employer furnished the care itself 'rather than paying you, or a provider you chose'.

unruled:f2441#9.evidence: f2441.line1_box checks the box and cites the statement requirement (i2441 p. 2, Line 1); which three providers are listed on the form and the attached statement's contents (name, SSN, the same columns for the others) are paper-filing instructions that change no amount.

unruled:f2441#10.evidence: f2441.line2_box checks the box, with a display note to attach a statement listing the other qualifying persons (i2441 p. 3, Line 2); the column (c) box is dependent.dc_line2c ('Check here if the qualifying person was over age 12 and was disabled', from dependent.dc_over12_care). Choosing the three people with the highest expenses for the form and the statement's contents change no amount.
